great model - the animation could be improved a little by studying the closest anatomical references available - Roadrunner, Cassowary etc. may be a useful reference. Although birds don't have long tails, ultimately the tail is just a counterbalance for a heavier neck and skull. What i'd change is the rocking motion forward and back like a ship in a heavy swell. Bipeds keep their body pretty stable, especially when moving fast. Although this is a herbivore, it's still likely to keep it's head almost motionless in XYZ space while moving, or otherwise shift often to different stable positions - a chicken doesn't actually bob it's head up and down - it snaps between different stable positions to give it a better sense of its surroundings. Predators keep their heads absolutely still - look at a cheetah in motion, or a hawk hovering. We don't have dinosaurs to use as reference material any more, but animals all have to solve the same problems of gravity/predators/prey and this will result in the same motions.
